Migration involves taking on new and dynamic risks and vulnerabilities in sustaining everyday social reproduction, especially for low-income migrants in developing countries and their families; these are inflected by gendered power relations and are specific to individual life-course transitions; and these risks and vulnerabilities are especially marked at life-course critical junctures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which migration shapes the social relations of social reproduction and how this is mediated through the gendered life course of individual and family members.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
migration is not only a process of social transformation but also a process of social reproduction.
social protection is a key element of social reproduction and is a central concern for migrants and their families.

social reproduction is a key concept for understanding migration and social protection, but that the concept needs to be developed further to capture more fully the dynamic and life-course nature of migration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
migration involves (and is shaped by) renegotiations of social reproduction.

the social protection of migrants and their families is a key issue for social policy, but it is also a challenge for the social sciences to better understand the complex and gendered dynamics of social reproduction.
migration and social reproduction are deeply interlinked, and that the interconnections and tensions between them are particularly marked at critical junctures in the life course.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social protection for migrants and their families should be conceptualised as part of social reproduction.

social protection needs to be more than just a safety net for migrants, and that it needs to be understood as part of the social reproduction of migrants and their families, rather than as a separate and distinct policy area.
social reproduction is a key lens through which to understand and analyse social protection for migrant households.
